case_name: State of Uttar Pradesh v Raj Nath and Others
facts: The deceased Sabha Shankar died of a gunshot wound in front of his house on August 13, 1968 at about 12.30 p.m.
The First Information Report (Ext. P-1) was lodged by P.W.-1 Amarnath, a distant collateral of the deceased, at Police Station, Mirzamurad on the same day at about 2.45 p.m.

According to the version of the eye-witnesses, on the day of occurrence P.W. 7 Shri Deo Murti Pandey, Advocate, appointed as a Commissioner, had come to the village from Varanasi to conduct a local inspection.
issues: Whether the testimony of the eye-witnesses should be relied upon
petitioner_arguments: The appellants are entitled to the benefit of doubt and deserve to be acquitted
court_reasoning: The High Court has made no attempt to come to grips with the evidence of the eye-witnesses.

It was not proper for the High Court to totally brush aside the testimony of the eye-witnesses without discussing the evidence and without coming to a conclusion whether they were trustworthy and reliable
holding: The judgment and order of the High Court are set aside
We direct the High Court to dispose of the appeal afresh, without being influenced by any of the observations made above.
cases_cited: State of Uttar Pradesh v Raj Nath
